newsitem.title: DENMARK: U.S. PPI pushes Danish shares to new heights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PPI pushes Danish shares to new heights.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at a record high for the second consecutive day on Wednesday, boosted by U.S. producer price data, and dealers expected further gains Thursday on the back of the rising Dow.
"The Danish stock market was trickling downward until the U.S. PPI numbers came along and moved the whole thing up," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index rose 0.87 point to 163.90 in overall bourse turnover of 1.08 million crowns. The KFX June future, however, fell 0.10 point to 163.15 with 1,910 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns, traded.
Novo Nordisk listed in Copenhagen and New York, was boosted both by better than expected first quarter earnings and by the U.S. data, dealers said.
It closed up 19 crowns at 703.00 crowns, close to its year high of 706.00.
News of the Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) alliance with five other airlines failed to impress the Copenhagen market and the carrier's share closed down 2.50 crowns at 68.50.
"Who says the new alliance will have any effect, the market must wait and see if there is any potential cost saving," a dealer said.
